name: Mackay
departure_points: Mackay Marina (Mackay Harbour)
Hay Point boat ramp (south of Mackay)
Seaforth, Victor Creek and Murray Creek (Mt Pelion) all-tide ramps for the Mackay Net Free Zone
Kinchant, Teemburra and Eungella dams (freshwater)

species_seasons.when: Year-round; during the 1 Nov–31 Jan saltwater closure anglers fish Teemburra, Kinchant and Eungella dams, focusing on afternoon, dusk and night bites
February to about May while water stays above ~24°C
From June as weather stabilises; August–September good for offshore jigging for fingermark, coral trout and nannygai
Winter influx
Around October, when they come inshore after bait schools

notes: The Mackay Net Free Zone runs from Cape Hillsborough to the northern end of St Helens Bay and takes in fifteen creek systems.
Offshore, the Sir James Smith Group (from Seaforth), Cumberland Islands (off Mackay) and Beverley Group (off Sarina) sit in about 30–40 m of water.

Scawfell Island is a common base for reef trips; large-mouth nannygai and red emperor start to appear in numbers as depths drop to about 50 m, and the 'Shipping Channel' area between Scawfell and Stevens/Credlin reefs is well known for red fish.
Square Reef, Stevens Reef and Chauvel Reef are popular Great Barrier Reef anchorages.
The Pioneer River runs through town; deep water near the Forgan Bridge and 'The Vee' at Bassett Basin produce barramundi.

name: Whitsundays
departure_points: Coral Sea Marina (Shingley Dr), Airlie Beach
Hamilton Island Marina
Cape Gloucester Resort (Hydeaway Bay)
Shute Harbour (no dedicated fishing operator confirmed)

species_seasons.when: Year-round, peak August to December

species_seasons.species: Coral reef fin fish (coral trout etc.) and Spanish mackerel
species_seasons.when: Regulated closures apply in October and November

species_seasons.species: Coral trout, red emperor, nannygai, sweetlip
species_seasons.when: Year-round reef targets

notes: Most fishing grounds around the Whitsunday Islands are 40–70 m deep.
The outer reef is about 40 nautical miles from Airlie Beach.
Some operators hold Yellow Zone (Great Barrier Reef Marine Park) access for areas others cannot fish.
Several Hamilton Island restaurants will cook guests' catch.

name: Bowen
departure_points: Bowen Boat Harbour ramp
Don River boat ramp (for northern creeks)
Beach ramps for Adelaide and Duck creeks (top of the tide only)

species_seasons.when: Year-round; barramundi closed season Nov–Feb (east coast closure 1 Nov–31 Jan)

notes: Bowen's creek systems hold healthy numbers of mangrove jack, bream, whiting and barramundi.

South of town, Adelaide and Duck creeks can be reached by sea only around the top of the tide via beach ramps; to the north, Bob Moses, Boat and Meatwork creeks are reached from the Don River ramp around high tide.
Many creeks become landlocked by tidal flats at low tide.

No Bowen-based fishing charter with its own website was found; Razorfish (Cape Gloucester) offers Bowen departures by arrangement and Bowen's tourism site points visitors to Whitsunday Fishing Charters at Airlie Beach.

name: Townsville
departure_points: Breakwater Marina, Mariners Drive, Townsville
Horseshoe Bay (Pacific Drive), Magnetic Island
Nelly Bay public boat ramp, Magnetic Island

species_seasons.when: Year-round day and night reef trips (weather permitting)
Trolled around Magnetic Island's bays

notes: Magnetic Island has 23 bays and beaches, 14 of them fishable, with shipwrecks, shoals, rocks, reefs and mangroves.
Offshore trips from Magnetic Island run up to 50 nautical miles to Great Barrier Reef shoal grounds.
From Breakwater Marina, larger charter boats reach the first reef drop in about 1.5–2 hours; trips of 12–23 hours are common for 'reds'.
Conquest Charters (Yeppoon-based) also lists day and night reef trips departing Breakwater Marina, Townsville, to reefs such as Centipede, Grub, Backnumbers, Braggs, Hopkinson and French reefs.

name: Hinchinbrook & Lucinda
departure_points: Lucinda boat ramps (Dungeness Road area)
Cardwell boat ramp
Port Hinchinbrook (no dedicated operator confirmed)

species_seasons.when: Main inshore targets in the Hinchinbrook Channel (barramundi closed 1 Nov–31 Jan)
Depending on the time of year, offshore from Lucinda

notes: Lucinda sits at the southern end of the Hinchinbrook Channel, about an hour and a half north of Townsville.
Small boats can reach the shallow creeks of Hinchinbrook Island and the mainland in Girringun National Park.
GT popping and stickbaiting can start close in, near the end of the Lucinda sugar loading jetty, before moving to island and reef grounds.
Inshore creek fishing is a sheltered option on windy days.

name: Mission Beach
departure_points: Clump Point boat ramp and jetty (no fishing-only operator confirmed)
Day trips with pick-up in Mission Beach (Cairns-based guides)

species_seasons.species: Barramundi, mangrove jack, queenfish, river GTs
species_seasons.when: Coastal rivers; operator lists July–October as prime multi-day season
Walk-and-wade in rainforest streams

notes: The Cassowary Coast around Mission Beach combines coastal rivers, World Heritage rainforest streams and tropical islands for sportfishing.
Mission Beach Charters, once listed for fishing, now focuses on snorkelling, island camping and transfers.
No Mission Beach-based fishing charter with a current website was found; Tropical Sportfisher (Cairns) runs day trips from Mission Beach and multi-day packages based there.

name: Cairns
departure_points: Marlin Marina, Pier Point Rd, Cairns City (D Finger; reef and estuary boats)
Tingira St boat ramp, Portsmith (small-boat estuary and reef trips)
Yorkeys Knob / Half Moon Bay (some game boats)
Accommodation pick-up for river, Lake Tinaroo and Mulgrave/Russell river trips

species_seasons.when: Early September to mid/end December, between Cairns and Lizard Island along the reef edge and continental shelf
Year-round within about an hour of Cairns; best March–September and December–January
Consistent year-round; bottom fishing can be less predictable in the wet season (Jan–Mar)
Often more active during the wet season (Jan–Mar)
May–August in the Mulgrave/Russell river system
September–December in the Mulgrave/Russell rivers; barramundi closed season 1 Nov–31 Jan on the east coast
Warmer months, October–April (fly trips); metre-plus fish

notes: Cairns is the base for the giant black marlin fishery on the 150-mile stretch of reef between Cairns and Lizard Island, fished mainly with trolled baits and tag-and-release on circle hooks.
Shared reef boats typically fish 30–60 m of water within about 50 km of Cairns, with travel of at least 90 minutes each way to the reef.
Trinity Inlet, the estuary right beside the city, is a State Marine Park with over 100 km of creeks and channels holding barramundi, jacks, fingermark and threadfin.
The Mulgrave and Russell rivers and Mutchero Inlet, about 40 km south, are a popular day-trip river system.
Lake Tinaroo on the Atherton Tablelands was the first stocked barramundi lake and is known for metre-plus impoundment barra.
Great Barrier Reef trips attract the Environmental Management Charge (reef tax), $8.50 per person from 1 April 2026.

name: Port Douglas
departure_points: Crystalbrook Superyacht Marina, 44 Wharf St
Marano's Fuel Wharf (berth 4)
Public jetty / boat ramp, Ashford Ave (behind St Mary's by the Sea)

species_seasons.when: July to October
September to mid December, Cairns to Lizard Island

species_seasons.species: Coral trout and other reef fin fish
species_seasons.when: Year-round except reef fin-fish spawning closures in October/November

notes: Reef fishing grounds off Port Douglas are generally about an hour's run away for the larger boats.
Dragon Lady reports travelling 20–25 miles to the outer reef (50–80 minutes) and 30+ miles to the continental shelf for game fishing.
Inshore options include the Port Douglas estuaries, fringing reefs and Low Isles.
Shared reef boats such as MV Norseman cap fishing numbers at 20.

name: Daintree
departure_points: Public wharf near the Daintree River Ferry Crossing, 315 Cape Tribulation Rd, Lower Daintree
Daintree River Ferry boat ramp (about 200 m before the ferry)

species_seasons.when: Caught on lure in every month; optimum September to March (outside the 1 Nov–31 Jan closed season)
When in season

notes: The Daintree River is the region's largest river, with over 25 km of navigable water lined by mangroves and World Heritage rainforest.
Islands, wrecks and inshore reefs at the river mouth, including Snapper Island, can be added on calm days.
The river holds plenty of saltwater crocodiles and rich birdlife, so many trips double as nature tours.

name: Cooktown & Lizard Island
departure_points: Cooktown waterfront / Endeavour River (Webber Esplanade)

species_seasons.when: September to mid/end December on the reef between Cairns and Lizard Island
Endeavour and Annan rivers (barramundi closed 1 Nov–31 Jan)

notes: Cooktown is the closest town to the Great Barrier Reef; Dawson Reef can be reached within about 10 minutes of leaving port.

Cape Bedford to the north offers mangroves for barra and jacks, poppers for GT and queenfish, and wrecks for fingermark and nannygai; Archer Point to the south leads to rainforest-meets-reef coastline.
Cooktown is about 320 km (4 hours) by sealed road from Cairns or a 40–45 minute flight.
The Lizard Island Black Marlin Classic is held in the region.

name: Weipa & Cape York
departure_points: Weipa (guides collect guests from accommodation)
Albatross Bay rivers: Mission, Embley, Wenlock/Archer systems

species_seasons.when: Most prolific April–July
Year-round, more inshore in winter
Late March to mid December; most operators do not run in the wet (Dec–Mar)

notes: Weipa sits on Albatross Bay on the Gulf side of Cape York, about an hour's flight from Cairns; daily flights make it one of the most accessible remote fishing towns.
Prevailing south-easterly winds blow offshore for about nine months of the year, keeping the Gulf side fishable.
Flats, beaches and headlands offer sight fishing for permit, golden trevally, queenfish, giant herring and tuna; rivers hold barramundi, threadfin and jacks.
Most visiting anglers book multi-day packages with accommodation, meals and transfers; much of the fishing is catch and release.
Weipa's local press describes its charter fleet as one of the biggest in Queensland.

name: Karumba & the Gulf
departure_points: Karumba (Norman River mouth)
Karumba Point

species_seasons.when: Dedicated barra charters run February–April and September to 7 October
Offshore trips 40–50 km into the Gulf, year-round weather permitting

notes: Estuary trips fish the sheltered Norman River and nearby creeks such as the Bynoe for barramundi, king and blue threadfin, black jewfish and grunter.
Barramundi cannot be targeted during the Gulf closed season.
Remote camping trips around Karumba and Normanton reach lightly fished rivers.
